alert.summary: CloudWatch alarm fired for ECS service checkout

root_cause.hypothesis: checkout pods OOMKilled: memory_limit_mib=48 far below app's ~900MiB cache alloc on startup. Logs show 'allocating 900MiB cache' right after 'memory pressure rising', both pods, then BackOff/CrashLoop. oom_killed_containers=2 matches pods_ready=0. Recent image bump (python:3.12-alpine → 3.12.7-alpine) coincides but unlikely cause itself — same base tier, no evidence of mem-limit change in that diff shown.
evidence: memory_limit_mib: 48 vs log line 'allocating 900MiB cache' — ~19x limit
WARN memory pressure rising precedes alloc line in both pods
BackOff events for both pod replicas, restart_count: 9
ruled_out: crashloop_containers: 0.0 — not yet in official crashloop state, still backoff/restart phase
image tag bump alone as root cause — no size/config change evidence tied to memory behavior; deploy timing correlates but mechanism unclear, kept as weak secondary factor not primary

proposal.reasoning: OOMKill root cause: memory_limit_mib=48 far below app's ~900MiB cache alloc at startup. Both pods die same way immediately after alloc, matches oom_killed_containers=2. No action in allowed set can raise the memory limit itself — restart_pods/scale_up/scale_down/rollback_deploy/failover_replica/clear_cache/terminate_connections don't touch the container memory limit config, so all would loop back into the same OOMKill. Recent image bump is coincidental per hypothesis, not the cause.
proposal.expected_effect: Human raises memory_limit_mib (e.g. to >=1024MiB) or reduces app's startup cache alloc; no remediation action here changes the underlying resource limit.
